tasks.short: Review competitive products and other art for ideas

steps.what: Review and evaluate competitive products
Log the products on the comparison sheet
Note music, television and other forms
Generate design ideas from the notes
Draft a card for the design ideas

loop.output: card that cites logged titles only
loop.check: Every cited title is on the comparison sheet
loop.stop: Stop if the idea id has no feature row
loop.why_not_simpler: The idea sentence is not a lookup, but it must not add a title

steps.what: Discuss the design ideas with a colleague
Sign the design ideas card

tasks.design: The designer logs title, medium and one noted feature on a {SPREADSHEET} kept with the notes in {DOCS}. A bounded idea card copies only those rows. Generating the new design idea stays with the designer, and only a signed card is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparisons were long notes, so an idea could not be traced to a product or a film the designer had actually seen.
tasks.enabler_now: A title and a feature can be fields, so the card can cite a row instead of a memory.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing what is worth taking from a film or a rival, and turning it into a game idea, is still judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides which feature is interesting and what the new idea actually is.

ambition.what: File one idea card after each review set, not a single yearly dump of references

tasks.altitude: Less time reformatting notes. Watching and inventing stay. The designer can reject a card that cites no title.

reach.task: Estimate a prototype of the signed idea
reach.learn: Which idea was signed and which references were only notes

evidence.claim: Designers review rival products and other art, then write notes. The new idea is not a summary of those notes. It is a separate judgement.
A card can cite a title the designer logged. It should not add a feature the designer did not write down.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends at a signed idea card. Prototyping the idea is a later task.

Input contract: title, medium as product or film or music or television or other, feature noted, why it mattered, and idea id. Producer is the game designer. A card may not cite a title that is not on the log. If the note is prose, the designer types title and feature and marks the row manual.

A sheet and a document template are configured first. Nothing watches a film or a rival on the designer behalf. The meeting prior overstates a standing meeting. Most of this task is solitary review plus one short discussion.
unknowns: Whether the studio may store notes about unreleased rival products.
Who else may add a title to the log.
research_questions: What share of idea notes name no title?
How often is a signed idea picked up in a prototype?

already_counted.description: Time spent evaluating products stays in the remaining work
Inventing the idea stays with the designer and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Drop comparison rows whose title no longer resolves and fix the card template

approvals.approved_version: idea card version signed after this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes notes stay as prose, so the card is written by hand. The high case assumes rows exist but the designer still watches the work and still invents the idea. Time spent playing or watching is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate with artists on the visual style

steps.what: Draft the visual style constraints

loop.input: style fields and the brief template
loop.output: brief that cites only submitted reference ids
loop.check: Every reference id in the brief was submitted
loop.stop: Stop if the palette intent is empty
loop.why_not_simpler: The wording of a do-not varies, but the brief must not add a reference

steps.what: Artists send reference images for the style
Check references against the style brief
Collaborate with artists on appropriate visual style
Sign how the team will achieve the style
File the signed style note

tasks.design: The designer enters style id, camera note, palette intent and a do-not on a {DOCS} template. A bounded brief drafts only from those fields. The work to achieve the style stays a meeting with artists, and the signed style note is what {PROJECT} shows as current.
tasks.previous_blocker: Style direction lived in chat threads and loose images, so an artist could build from a reference the designer had dropped.
tasks.enabler_now: A style id can tie a reference, a do-not and a decision together.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a picture is the right style is a shared judgement in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides what is appropriate and when an artist push should change the style.

ambition.what: Sign a style note whenever the references change, not only at the art kickoff

tasks.altitude: The collaboration stays weekly. The brief is no longer rebuilt from chat. The designer can reject a reference that is not on the signed note.

reach.task: Paint only from the signed style note
reach.learn: Which references are allowed and which do-nots are in force

evidence.claim: Visual style work in a mid-size studio is a meeting with artists plus a pile of references. The appropriate look is agreed in the room, not in a template.
A brief can list camera, palette intent and a do-not from fields. It does not choose the style.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the signed style note is filed. Producing the art is the artist task.

Input contract: style id, camera note, palette intent, do-not text, reference id, and decision. Producer of the constraints is the game designer. Producer of the reference id is the artist. A reference with no id is not cited. Chat images are registered by hand and marked manual.
The document template and the project board status are configured before custom code. Artist drawing time is outside this task. The design does not score artists.
unknowns: Whether some artists are freelancers rather than staff.
Who breaks a tie if an art director is not the designer.
research_questions: What share of style chats never become a note?
How often is a signed do-not still violated?

already_counted.description: Designer edits a do-not the draft worded too broadly
Time in the style meeting stays with the designer and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Update the style template when a new do-not field is needed
Artists re-register a reference the form rejected

approvals.approved_version: style note signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes references stay in chat, so the brief is written by hand. The high case assumes fields exist but every style meeting still happens and the designer still decides. Artist drawing time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write game dialogue and supervise the writing

steps.what: Set speaker, scene and intent for the writing
Write dialogue lines into the scene script

loop.input: scene fields and the line template
loop.output: lines tagged with scene id and speaker id
loop.check: Each line uses a speaker id that is on the scene
loop.stop: One draft, then leave a blank if the intent is empty
loop.why_not_simpler: Line wording is not a fixed phrase list, but the speaker must not change

steps.what: Writer revises dialogue the designer marked
Supervise the writing in review
Sign the dialogue script version
Store the signed dialogue script

tasks.design: Scene id, speaker, intent and a banned phrase are fields on a {DOCS} template. A bounded draft writes dialogue lines that must use those fields and must not add a speaker. The designer supervises the writing, signs one script version, and only that version is stored for the build.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lines were rewritten in long documents, so a draft could put words in the mouth of the wrong speaker.
tasks.enabler_now: Speaker and intent can be fields a line must cite, which a template can check.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a line sounds like the character, and whether it may be said, is still the designer call.
tasks.human_edge: The designer keeps the voice and rejects a line that is merely grammatical.

ambition.what: Sign dialogue per scene when the intent changes, not in one late script pass

tasks.altitude: First drafts of lines take less blank-page time. Supervision and the signature stay. The designer can refuse a line whose speaker is not on the scene.

reach.task: Hook the signed dialogue to the scene
reach.learn: Which script version is signed and which lines were rejected

evidence.claim: Game text and dialogue in a mid-size studio are drafted, then supervised, then revised. Tone and canon are the hard part, not the page layout.
A template can propose a line from speaker and intent. A fluent line can still be wrong for the character, so the designer signs the script before it is stored.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the signed script version is stored. Recording a voice performance is out of scope.

Input contract: scene id, speaker id, intent, banned phrase, line text, and writer id. Producer of the intent is the game designer. Producer of a first human line may be a writer. A line with no scene id or no speaker id is not drafted and not signed. If the intent is only in a meeting, the designer types it and marks it manual.
The document template is used before custom code. The draft may not invent a speaker or a scene. Unsigned lines are not stored for the build.
unknowns: Whether a separate writer is on staff for this title.
Which languages must be authored here rather than translated later.
research_questions: What share of lines change after the first review?
How often does a line cite the wrong speaker?

already_counted.description: Designer rewrites lines that miss the character voice
Supervision time stays in the review and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Update speaker ids and banned phrases when the cast changes
Writer revises a line the template left blank

approvals.approved_version: dialogue script version signed for this scene
the same signed dialogue script version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes intent stays as prose, so lines are still written by hand and the template does not fill. The high case assumes fields exist but every scene is still supervised and signed. Voice recording is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult stakeholders on requirements for online features

steps.what: Submit asks for online features
Consult multiple stakeholders on the ask
Define requirements from the meeting notes

loop.output: requirement rows that cite a feature id
loop.check: Every row cites a feature id from the form
loop.stop: Leave the row blank if a note names no feature id
loop.why_not_simpler: The rule sentence varies and is not a fixed lookup

steps.what: Comment on whether the requirements fit
Choose which online features to implement
File the signed requirements version

tasks.design: Stakeholders submit feature id, user, rule and platform limit on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded list in {DOCS} turns the meeting notes into requirement rows that must cite a feature id. The consult stays a meeting. The designer signs which online features to implement, and that version is the one {PROJECT} tracks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were rewritten from meeting notes, so a feature could be implemented that nobody had actually agreed.
tasks.enabler_now: A feature id and a rule can be fields, so a row can be checked against the form.
tasks.still_hard: Getting stakeholders to agree, and what to drop, is still a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides which online feature is in scope when stakeholders disagree.

ambition.what: Re-sign the online scope when a stakeholder changes a requirement, not only at kickoff

tasks.altitude: The meetings stay. The requirement list is no longer retyped from notes. The designer can refuse a feature that has no signed rule.

reach.task: Implement only the signed online features
reach.learn: Which feature ids are in scope and which rules are still open

evidence.claim: Defining online features in a mid-size studio is a set of stakeholder meetings plus a requirements list. Agreement is the hard part.
Rows can be arranged from notes that already name a feature id. A form does not create the agreement.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the signed requirements version is filed. Building the feature is the developer task.

Input contract: feature id, stakeholder role, user type, rule, platform limit, and in-scope flag. Producer of the ask is the stakeholder through the form. Producer of the in-scope flag is the game designer. A row with no feature id is not filed. If the meeting has no form, the designer types the rule and marks it manual.
The workflow form and the document template are configured before custom code. Nothing is sent to an outside platform from this task. Player account data is out of scope.
unknowns: Which stakeholders are a publisher or a platform rather than staff.
Whether any online feature takes a payment.
research_questions: What share of features in the build have no signed rule?
How often does scope change after kickoff?

already_counted.description: Designer rewrites requirement rows the notes did not support
Consult time stays in the meeting and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Keep platform-limit values aligned when a platform rule changes
Producer corrects an ask the form rejected

approvals.approved_version: requirements version signed for this scope decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes meetings leave only prose, so requirements are still written by hand. The high case assumes the form is used but every consult still happens and the designer still sets scope. Developer build time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Idea cards and dialogue lines start from fields the designer set. Style meetings and stakeholder meetings stay. The designer signs the idea, the style, the script and the online scope.
reach: Software developers receive the signed dialogue script and the signed online scope instead of a chat summary.
Artists receive the signed style note and the references that are actually allowed.
skills_to_grow: State a scene as speaker, intent and a banned phrase before any line is drafted.
Tie a style reference to a do-not a brief can check.
Write an online rule as a feature id a developer can build or refuse.
role.ambitious_version: Each scene has a signed script, each style change has a signed note, and an online feature without a signed rule is not built.
